time_precision: Actual host clock at creation; frozen before any worker computation for this target.
target: Decide existence of a Bhaskar Rao design BRD(26,130,25,5,4): a 26-by-130 matrix over {-1,0,1} with exactly 25 nonzero entries in every row, exactly 5 nonzero entries in every column, and, for every pair of distinct rows, exactly two columns where their product is +1, exactly two where it is -1, and 126 where it is 0.

The May paper (section 3.1, per CPro1OpenScreen) says the open lists come from the Handbook (V.4) with literature-solved instances omitted. The Handbook table and Chaudhry-Greig-Seberry, J. Statist. Plann. Inference 106 (2002) 303-327 (likely source of the exceptions) were NOT accessible (ScienceDirect/ResearchGate 403). A search miss is not novelty.
primary_attestation.definition: As in the CPro1 problem_def (identical to the standard BRD(v,k,lambda) with b = lambda v(v-1)/(k(k-1)) blocks): the absolute-value matrix is the incidence matrix of a 2-(26,5,4) design (repeated blocks allowed) and the signed inner product of any two distinct rows is 0 with exactly lambda/2 = 2 products of each sign.
primary_attestation.information_science_scope: Finite signed incidence structure (Bhaskar Rao design / orthogonal signing of a BIBD); used in weighing-matrix and code constructions.

parent_lead_untrusted: [INFERENCE] vr = 650 = bk; lambda(v-1) = 100 = r(k-1); b = lambda v(v-1)/(k(k-1)) = 130. Natural restricted models: points Z13 x {0,1} with 10 base blocks under Z13 (CPro1OpenScreen); points Z26 with 5 base blocks; Z5- or Z25+infinity-based models; two-phase search (2-(26,5,4) design first, then signing). The BTD(14,28) witness in this run came from a small cyclic invariant model, so restricted orbit models are a reasonable first lever; a restricted miss is never an exclusion.

exact_quantifiers.matrix: All 26x130 matrices over {-1,0,1}; repeated columns allowed; no automorphism, cyclicity, resolvability or prescribed base-block assumption in the target.
exact_quantifiers.symmetries: Row/column permutations and multiplying any row or any column by -1 preserve validity. Further reductions require a written completeness argument before any exclusion claim.

first_obligations: Freeze README attack/representation before substantial search; earlier lanes read-only.

Strict definition-first stdlib witness verifier plus an independent native or second checker, calibrated with known BRDs (e.g. the CPro1 dev instances or small textbook BRD(v,3,2)/(v,4,2)) and intended-reason mutations.
Pursue restricted orbit models and two-phase (design then signing) search; any nonexistence direction needs a written proof and checked certificates.

acceptance.existence: One strict-format matrix (line 1: BRD 26 130 25 5 4, then exactly 26 lines of 130 space-separated entries from {-1,0,1}, final LF) passing the parent definition-first checker, two independently authored checker routes, intended-reason controls and producer/seed replay.
acceptance.nonexistence: A written mathematical contradiction or complete unrestricted case split with correctness proof, AND an independently checked DRAT/LRAT or equivalent exact machine-checked proof. Interrupted checks are UNKNOWN.
acceptance.claim: Settles one explicitly listed finite existence case only; any spectrum consequence needs the inaccessible primary source and is reported separately.
